answers.how: The ball diameter is about 36 px, giving 0.21/36 m per pixel. A quadratic fit to its center positions gives about 541 px/s at 0.5 s.
The fitted trajectory gives a deceleration magnitude of about 59.4 px/s². Converting with the ball's diameter gives 0.35 m/s².
The fitted trajectory gives about 511 px/s at 1 s. Using 0.21/36 m per pixel gives 2.98 m/s.
The pre-impact trajectory has approximately constant deceleration, with magnitude 59.4 px/s², equivalent to 0.35 m/s².
An upright pin is about 55 px tall, versus the ball's 36 px diameter: 55 × 0.21/36 ≈ 0.32 m.
